sections.h2: Who records a deed in Belmont County, Ohio?
sections.html:
The Belmont County Recorder files deeds, mortgages and related papers in the courthouse at 101 West Main Street, St. Clairsville. The recorder describes the job as keeping the county's land records accurate, indexed and open to the public, with more than 220 years of them on hand. The staff will explain how the records are organized but will not run a title search for you.

Indexing is the part sellers rarely notice. Each document is indexed so that a searcher can build a chain of title, which shows every owner and every debt attached to the land. Accurate indexing is what lets a title searcher find a deed, a lien or a release later.

Belmont County was organized in November 1801 and named St. Clairsville its seat in 1803, so the books reach back more than two centuries. Wikipedia places the county along the Ohio River, and the recorder's own description of the work includes farm deeds, home mortgages, oil and gas leases and military discharge papers.

sections.h2: What does the Belmont County Recorder charge to record a document?
sections.html:
The recorder's online calculator states a simple structure that follows Ohio Revised Code 317.32. Belmont County does not add the optional $5 document preservation fee, which the statute lets a county charge.

Belmont County Recorder fee structure
ServiceFee
First two pages of a document$34
Each additional page$8
Each indexed marginal notation (reference)$4
Document that misses the layout standard$20 extra

Source: Belmont County Recorder fee calculator.

The statute splits the first-two-page fee into a $17 base fee and a $17 housing trust fund fee. Each added page carries a $4 base and a $4 trust fund share. The statute sends any preservation surcharge to the county general fund, and the trust fund share is collected under section 317.36. Other services carry their own statutory rates:

  • Certified copy: a $1 base fee and a $1 trust fund fee per page, plus 50 cents and 50 cents when the recorder's seal is needed.
  • Photocopy at the counter: $1 and $1 per page.
  • Each marginal reference: $2 and $2, which matches the $4 in the table.
  • Living will or health care power of attorney: a base fee of $17 to $20 plus a matching trust fund fee.

Fees are due when the paper is presented, though electronic recording customers may pay by electronic funds transfer or ACH after presentation. The calculator is the quickest way to price a deed with several pages of legal description.

sections.h2: What layout rules apply to a deed recorded in Belmont County?
sections.html:
Documents must meet the standards in section 317.114, which the recorder summarizes on its document standards page. A document that does not conform can still be recorded, but the office collects an additional $20.

  • Type no smaller than 10 point.
  • Paper no smaller than 8 1/2 by 11 inches and no larger than 8 1/2 by 14.
  • Black or blue ink only, and no highlighting.
  • A 3-inch margin at the top of the first page and 1 1/2 inches at the top of later pages.
  • A 1-inch margin on each side and at the bottom.

The rules do not apply to papers from a court or taxing authority, plats, exhibits, DD-214 discharge papers, state or federal documents, or any document signed before the law took effect in July 2009.

sections.h2: What documents does a Belmont County recorder have to file?
sections.html:
Section 317.08 lists what goes into the official records, and the list explains why more than deeds pass through the counter. Items most relevant to a house sale include:

  • Deeds and other instruments that convey land outright.
  • Mortgages, with their amendments, modifications and extensions.
  • Executory installment contracts for land that run more than a year.
  • Options to purchase, which must state a specific day and year of expiration.
  • Powers of attorney and memoranda of trust.
  • Declarations and bylaws for condominiums under Chapter 5311.
  • Easements, environmental covenants and conservation easements under the listed statutes.

For a seller the important point is that a recorded mortgage, option or contract stays in the public record until a release or other instrument is recorded against it. Ask a title company to check the county's records for a paid-off mortgage whose release was never recorded.

sections.h2: What steps come before the recorder in Belmont County?
sections.html:
The auditor's office sits in the same courthouse and acts on the deed. Under section 319.202, the auditor does not endorse a deed until the grantee or a representative submits a statement declaring the value of the property, or a statement of the reason for exemption. The deed transfer desk takes calls at 740-699-2136, and the real estate desk at 740-699-2132.

A common order in Ohio counties, which Belmont County's offices can confirm, runs like this:

  • Prepare the deed with a full legal description and parcel number.
  • Take the deed and value statement to the auditor, pay the conveyance fee and get the endorsement.
  • Present the endorsed deed to the recorder with the fee.
  • Receive the recorded original or a return by mail.

Ask the auditor's deed transfer desk for the current conveyance rate, since counties set their own transfer tax within the limit in the statute. Ask the recorder's staff whether the recorded deed can be returned by mail.

sections.h2: What should a Belmont County seller know about the local market?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau reports a median owner-occupied home value of $154,900 for 2020 to 2024 and an owner-occupied rate of 73.6 percent. Of residents age one and older, 90.9 percent lived in the same house a year earlier, which points to long ownership and, in many cases, deeds that are decades old. The 2020 census counted 31,618 housing units, and 13.6 percent of them stood vacant. Median monthly owner costs run $1,215 with a mortgage and $489 without one, and 24.9 percent of residents are 65 or older.

The county's estimated population fell 3.1 percent between April 2020 and July 2025. The county's protected areas include Barkcamp State Park, Dysart Woods and the Egypt Valley Wildlife Area, and its lakes include Piedmont Lake and Belmont Lake. A house near any of them is sold on the same recorded title as one in town.

If a deed has gaps, such as a missing heir or a lien never released, the recorder cannot fix it. Resolve it with a title company or an attorney before recording a new deed.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Belmont County?
faqs.a: The recorder's calculator lists $34 for the first two pages and $8 for each additional page. A $4 fee applies to each indexed reference, and a document that misses the layout standard costs $20 more. The county does not add the optional $5 preservation fee.

faqs.q: Where is the Belmont County Recorder's office?
faqs.a: The office is in the courthouse at 101 West Main Street in St. Clairsville, Ohio 43950, the same building as the auditor and treasurer. Deed transfers start at the auditor's desk, which takes calls at 740-699-2136.

faqs.q: What paper size and ink does the recorder require?
faqs.a: Use 8 1/2 by 11 or 8 1/2 by 14 paper, a font of at least 10 point, and black or blue ink with no highlighting. Leave a 3-inch top margin on the first page, 1 1/2 inches on later pages and 1 inch elsewhere. Otherwise the office charges an extra $20.

faqs.q: Does the recorder search my title?
faqs.a: No. The recorder's staff will explain how the records are arranged but will not perform title searches. A title company or attorney does that work, and a lender or buyer will ask for it before closing.

faqs.q: Do I need the auditor before I record a Belmont County deed?
faqs.a: Yes, start with the auditor. Under section 319.202 the auditor's endorsement depends on a statement of value or a statement of the reason for exemption. Ask the recorder's staff how an endorsed deed should be delivered.
